title: Protecting the ports that face users
summary: Harden user-facing switch ports with fast start, BPDU guard and port security, and keep the uplink untouched.
objectives: Enable fast start and BPDU guard on edge ports only
Limit how many MAC addresses a user port accepts

tasks.title: Fast start on the edge ports
tasks.description: GE0/0/1 and GE0/0/2 connect single hosts, so they can go to forwarding at once. GE0/0/24 is the uplink to another switch and must not.
hints: A port that leads to another switch has to take part in the spanning tree calculation.
Example: interface GE0/0/1, then portfast enable

criteria.label: Fast start is on for GE0/0/1
Fast start is on for GE0/0/2
Fast start is off for the uplink GE0/0/24

tasks.title: Guard the edge ports
tasks.description: A user should never connect a switch. Turn on BPDU guard on the two edge ports so a switch plugged in there shuts the port down. The uplink must stay unguarded.
hints: BPDUs are the messages switches send to each other for spanning tree. A host never sends them.
Example: interface GE0/0/1, then bpdu guard enable

criteria.label: BPDU guard is on for GE0/0/1
BPDU guard is on for GE0/0/2
BPDU guard is off for the uplink GE0/0/24

tasks.title: Limit the MAC addresses
tasks.description: On GE0/0/1 allow exactly one MAC address, so a small switch or hub cannot be hidden behind the port.
hints: Port security has to be turned on before its limit has any effect.
Example: interface GE0/0/1, then port-security enable, then port-security max-mac-num 1

criteria.label: Port security on GE0/0/1 allows one MAC address
